title: AI Readiness Score™
tagline: How ready is your business to profit from AI? Find your score and your quick wins.
description: 12 questions that measure how your business uses AI and automation today — and reveal the quick wins that could save you hours every week.

categories.label: Current AI Usage
categories.recommendation: Pick one daily task (emails, proposals, social posts) and use AI for it every day this week. Consistency beats experiments.

categories.label: Automation
categories.recommendation: Connect your two most-used tools with Zapier or Make so information moves without copy-paste.

categories.label: Processes
categories.recommendation: Write down your 3 most repeated processes as simple checklists — AI and automation can only follow processes that exist on paper.

categories.label: Team Adoption
categories.recommendation: Name an 'AI champion' on your team and run a 30-minute weekly share of what worked. Adoption spreads through wins, not mandates.

questions.text: How often does anyone in your business use AI tools like ChatGPT or Claude?

options.label: Once in a while, out of curiosity
Daily — it's part of how we operate

questions.text: Which best describes what you use AI for today?

options.label: Embedded in client work, marketing and operations

questions.text: Do you use AI anywhere in your customer communication (drafting replies, chat, follow-ups)?

options.label: We've tested it once or twice
Yes — AI drafts or handles a large share of it

questions.text: How much of your admin work (scheduling, invoicing, data entry) is automated?
When a new lead comes in, what happens automatically?

options.label: Nothing — someone has to notice it
Auto-reply plus it's logged in our CRM
Auto-reply, CRM entry and a follow-up sequence starts

questions.text: Do your core tools (email, calendar, CRM, accounting) share data automatically?

options.label: No — we re-type things between tools

questions.text: Are your key business processes written down?

options.label: No — they live in people's heads

questions.text: How organized is your business data (client info, files, project history)?
Could you hand a repeat task to a new assistant (human or AI) with written instructions today?

options.label: No — I'd have to explain everything live

questions.text: How does your team feel about AI?
Has anyone in the business been given time or training to learn AI tools?

options.label: They explore on their own time
Yes — dedicated time and clear expectations

questions.text: Is there a clear owner for improving tools and automation in your business?

options.label: Yes — a clear owner with time allocated

bands.label: Pre-AI — Big wins waiting
bands.summary: Your business hasn't started its AI journey — which means the easiest, highest-return wins are all still on the table. Businesses at this stage typically reclaim 5–10 hours a week within their first month of adopting basic AI and automation.
actionPlan: Week 1: Create a free ChatGPT or Claude account and use it daily for emails and writing.
Week 1: List every task you repeat more than 3 times a week.
Week 2: Set up online booking and an email auto-reply for new inquiries.
Week 2: Choose one simple CRM and put every lead in it.
Week 3: Use AI to draft one week of marketing content in a single sitting.
Week 3: Document your most repeated process as a checklist.
Week 4: Automate one workflow end-to-end with Zapier or Make.
Week 4: Book an AI Audit to build your personal AI roadmap.

bands.label: Experimenting — Time to systematize
bands.summary: You've dabbled with AI, but it isn't saving you real hours yet. The gap between 'playing with ChatGPT' and 'AI-powered business' is process — and you're one focused month away from closing it.
actionPlan: Week 1: Pick your 3 most time-consuming weekly tasks and write an AI-assisted workflow for each.
Week 1: Create saved prompts/templates so good AI outputs are repeatable.
Week 2: Automate lead capture: every inquiry gets an instant reply and lands in your CRM.
Week 2: Connect two tools that currently require manual copy-paste.
Week 3: Introduce AI to one client-facing deliverable (proposals, reports, summaries).
Week 3: Run a 30-minute team session sharing what's working.
Week 4: Measure hours saved and pick the next 2 automations.
Week 4: Book an AI Audit to prioritize by return on effort.

bands.label: Adopting — Ahead of most competitors
bands.summary: You're genuinely ahead of the pack. AI and automation are working for you — now the opportunity is depth: connecting systems, standardizing prompts and letting AI touch revenue-generating work, not just admin.
actionPlan: Week 1: Map every process AI touches today and score each by hours saved.
Week 1: Identify your one workflow still fully manual — that's this month's target.
Week 2: Build a shared prompt library so the whole team gets expert-level outputs.
Week 2: Add AI to your sales process: call prep, proposal drafts, follow-up personalization.
Week 3: Pilot an AI chatbot or assistant trained on your own FAQs and documents.
Week 3: Set an adoption metric (e.g. 'AI used in 80% of proposals').
Week 4: Review results and lock the wins into documented process.
Week 4: Book an AI Audit to find advanced plays your competitors haven't discovered.

bands.label: AI-Powered — Build your moat
bands.summary: Elite territory. AI is woven into how your business runs. Your next frontier is competitive advantage: custom AI assistants on your own data, AI-enhanced service delivery and scale without proportional headcount.
actionPlan: Week 1: Audit your AI stack for overlap and consolidate tools.
Week 1: Identify your highest-margin service and design an AI-enhanced version of it.
Week 2: Build a knowledge base so AI can answer from YOUR business data.
Week 2: Automate your reporting: numbers collected, summarized and delivered weekly by AI.
Week 3: Test an AI-first version of one client deliverable and compare quality and speed.
Week 3: Document your AI playbook so it survives team changes.
Week 4: Explore productizing your AI-enhanced expertise as a new offer.
Week 4: Book an AI Audit for an outside perspective on what's next.
